questions.question: When your motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, what can you do?

options.text: Apply the front brake harder.
Use less pressure on the front brake.
Apply the rear brake harder.
Lose traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward during braking, the front wheel gains more grip. This means you can press the front brake harder without losing control.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while braking on dry pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly apply it again.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If the rear wheel locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle will still be safe if it stays upright and goes in a straight line.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily buildup. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid this oily strip when it rains.
Ride only on the oily strip because it grips better.
Stay away from the entire center of the lane.
Do not worry about oil in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid this oily strip when it rains.
questions.explanation: Oil drips from vehicles and builds up in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this strip still has enough grip for motorcycles. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it and still stay in the center lane.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: At speeds faster than 55 mph.
After riding for several hours.
On short trips.
On long trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips (less than five miles) at slow speeds (less than 30 mph).

questions.question: When turning, how should you look through the turn?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes, not your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Always look through a turn toward where you want to go. Move only your head to look, keep your shoulders still, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: In hot weather, is it good to wear a riding jacket?

options.text: Yes, it helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
No, it can cause heat-related problems.
Only if the jacket is light-colored.
No, it is not important.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, in addition to providing crash protection.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left portion.
The center portion.
The right portion.
The shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of the lane when passing. This helps you see ahead better and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Do you need hearing protection when wearing a helmet?

options.text: No, the helmet is enough.
Yes, you need it in addition to a helmet.
Only on windy days.
No, not if you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you need it in addition to a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet on. Hearing protection lets you stay safe while still hearing important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: How often will you hear a tire going flat?

options.text: Always.
Usually.
Frequently.
Seldom.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom.
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. You are more likely to notice a flat tire by how your motorcycle handles.

questions.question: What following distance should you keep from other vehicles under normal conditions?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum four-second distance behind other vehicles under normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should a motorcycle rider do about this?

options.text: Slow down when riding at night.
Use the horn repeatedly when riding at night.
Do not ride at night.
Ride directly in front of another vehicle so its headlights show you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when riding at night.
questions.explanation: Safe night riding means slowing down, staying farther behind other vehicles, using the lights of cars ahead to see the road, using your high beam headlight (unless meeting or following another vehicle), and changing your lane position as needed.

questions.question: What should you do if your front wheel starts to skid?

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged and ride out the skid.
Keep the front brake engaged and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away and press it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and press it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake completely right away. Then press it again smoothly.

questions.question: What should you do on a long motorcycle trip?

options.text: Try to take as few breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel sleepy.
Wear warm clothing to stay comfortable during the ride.
Plan to ride more than 12 hours per day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear warm clothing to stay comfortable during the ride.
questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue on long trips, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use stimulants—they cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: When following another vehicle, should you ride on the far side of your lane?

options.text: Yes, because drivers will see you easily.
No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Yes, because a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
No, because it is illegal to ride on the far side of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of your lane where the driver is most likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: How should you use the handlebars to turn a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handlebar grip opposite the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the grips because it can be dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When riding faster than a walk, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pressing the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn causes the motorcycle to lean the right way.

questions.question: What should you do if it starts raining while you ride?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Speed up.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil buildup that makes it slippery when wet. When rain starts, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Slow down on wet roads.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another rider on the left, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the right side of your lane so they see you in their side mirror.
On the left side of your lane to see better ahead.
In the center of your lane so they see you in their rearview mirror.
Move side to side in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of your lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Before passing on the left, ride on the left side of your lane to see farther ahead and be more visible to drivers in the passing lane. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The center of the lane
The right side of the lane
It depends on the riding conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the riding conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Choose a lane position based on your current conditions. Make sure you have enough space around you and that other drivers can see you.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you tell them NOT to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as close to the front as possible without bothering you.
Hold onto your waist, hips, or belt tightly.
Talk or move around whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk or move around whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should stay quiet and still so you can focus on riding. Passengers should only get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as comfortable and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, what formation should you use?

options.text: Staggered formation.
Pyramid formation.
Single-file line.
Row of pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file line.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation works well for two-wheeled motorcycles, but three-wheeled motorcycles are too wide for this. Riders on three-wheeled motorcycles should ride in a single-file line.

questions.question: Before entering a left curve, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Usually ride in the right portion of the lane.
Usually ride in the left portion of the lane.
Always ride in the middle of the lane.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually ride in the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the right portion of your lane to see oncoming traffic as early as possible. This helps you position yourself better before the curve. Always be ready to adjust your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist prevent other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Riding in the left portion of a lane.
Riding in the center portion of a lane.
Giving dirty looks if another driver moves into their lane.
Riding in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle operator do on a slippery surface?

options.text: Not use the front brake.
Make sudden moves.
Brake frequently.
Reduce their speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Avoid making sudden movements. Use both brakes when stopping or slowing, even on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.
